title: A bell has been ringing since 1840. You can barely hear it
hook: An Oxford bell has rung twice a second for 186 years

open.title: The 186-year-old bell you can barely hear
open.line: Near the entrance of Oxford's physics lab sits a glass cabinet.

summary: A bell in Oxford's Clarendon Laboratory has run on two batteries since 1840. It has rung about 10 billion times.

text: Inside a glass case at Oxford's physics lab,
a tiny ball swings between two bells almost nonstop.
It hits a bell twice every second.
The label, in a professor's handwriting, says Set up in 1840.

panels.text: Wait, I can barely hear it.

text: Two layers of glass muffle the sound.
It's a bell you watch more than hear.
Actually, the whole thing runs on two batteries.
Each bell hangs under one of those columns. Those are the batteries.
The ball picks up charge from one bell, gets pushed away, and flies to the other.
It moves so little charge that the batteries barely drain.
The batteries are coated in melted sulfur.
What is inside the batteries is still just a guess.
It stops once the charge evens out, or the ball wears down.
So far it has rung about 10 billion times.
Guinness lists it as the world's most durable battery.

sources: Oxford University Physics: Exhibit 1, The Clarendon Dry Pile
